key_insight: The paper stabilizes neural constitutive modeling by combining a multi-mode RUDE backbone with conditioning, thermodynamic constraints, and an interpretable summary of learned tensor contributions.
engineering_relevance: It enables reliable, data-driven rheology models that can be used in CFD and process design for complex soft materials under unseen flow conditions.
method: Log-compress input invariants and use a split-network architecture to improve training conditioning.
Add a differentiable projection layer to enforce the Clausius–Duhem inequality at every time step.
Introduce the “rheome” to compactly visualize dominant weighted tensor-basis contributions.
evidence_signal: The framework was trained on LAOS data and validated on both synthetic multi-mode Giesekus data and experimental entangled silicone polymer melt data, where it stayed stable and accurate on unseen shear, stress-growth, and extensional flows.
watch_item: The added constraints and projection layer improve robustness, but implementation may be more complex and performance still depends on the quality and breadth of the training data.
paper_title: Stable and Interpretable Multi-Mode Rheological Universal Differential Equations (mmRUDEs) for Data-Driven Constitutive Modeling
